chapters.title: The Most Embarrassing Day of My Life

scenes.title: 7:43 a.m.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: By Friday afternoon, I was going to be the most popular kid at Westfield Middle School.
segments.display:
By Friday afternoon, I was going to be the most popular kid at Westfield Middle
School.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: By Friday afternoon, I was also going to lose my best friend.
segments.display: By Friday afternoon, I was also going to lose my best friend.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: But at 7:43 that morning, I didn't know either of those things.
segments.display: But at 7:43 that morning, I didn't know either of those things.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I was too busy trying to get a Pop-Tart out of a vending machine.
segments.display: I was too busy trying to get a Pop-Tart out of a vending machine.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I slammed my palm against the glass.
segments.display: I slammed my palm against the glass.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: The Pop-Tart hung from its metal coil, halfway to freedom.
segments.display: The Pop-Tart hung from its metal coil, halfway to freedom.

segments.speaker: JUNE
segments.text: You're negotiating with a vending machine again?
segments.display: You're negotiating with a vending machine again?

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I turned. June Park stood behind me, holding two chocolate milks.
segments.display: I turned. June Park stood behind me, holding two chocolate milks.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: It's not negotiating. It's psychological warfare.
segments.display: It's not negotiating. It's psychological warfare.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: June reached around me, pressed the refund button, and the Pop-Tart dropped.
segments.display: June reached around me, pressed the refund button, and the Pop-Tart dropped.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I stared at it. She handed me a chocolate milk.
segments.display: I stared at it. She handed me a chocolate milk.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: That was June. My best friend since third grade. She was smart, sarcastic, and possibly the only person alive who could beat me at Mario Kart while eating a bowl of cereal.
segments.display:
That was June. My best friend since third grade. She was smart, sarcastic, and
possibly the only person alive who could beat me at Mario Kart while eating a
bowl of cereal.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: She was also the reason I was about to make the dumbest decision of my thirteen years on Earth.
segments.display:
She was also the reason I was about to make the dumbest decision of my thirteen
years on Earth.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I just didn't know it yet.
segments.display: I just didn't know it yet.

scenes.music: playful, bouncy middle school comedy theme, pizzicato strings, light drums, ukulele; a morning full of mischief

scenes.title: First period

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: The announcement came during first period.
segments.display: The announcement came during first period.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: The voice belonged to Harper Blake, eighth grader, student council president, and a person so popular that people actually moved out of her way in the hallway.
segments.display:
The voice belonged to Harper Blake, eighth grader, student council president,
and a person so popular that people actually moved out of her way in the
hallway.

segments.speaker: HARPER
segments.text: As you know, today is our annual Friday Showcase! And this year, we'll be choosing a brand-new host for Wildcat Weekly!
segments.display:
As you know, today is our annual Friday
Showcase! And this year, we'll be choosing a brand-new host for Wildcat Weekly!

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Wildcat Weekly was our school's Friday video announcement show. Whoever hosted it got to interview students, make jokes, and appear on every television in the building.
segments.display:
Wildcat Weekly was our school's Friday video announcement show. Whoever hosted
it got to interview students, make jokes, and appear on every television in the
building.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I'd been dreaming about that job since sixth grade.
segments.display: I'd been dreaming about that job since sixth grade.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Mostly because, in sixth grade, I'd accidentally dumped an entire carton of orange juice down my pants at lunch.
segments.display:
Mostly because, in sixth grade, I'd accidentally dumped an entire carton of
orange juice down my pants at lunch.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: People had called me Juice Boy for seven months.
segments.display: People had called me Juice Boy for seven months.

segments.speaker: HARPER
segments.text: Finalists, remember to submit your audition reels by lunch. We'll announce the winner at this afternoon's assembly!
segments.display:
Finalists, remember to submit your audition
reels by lunch. We'll announce the winner at this afternoon's assembly!

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I turned to June. She smiled.
segments.display: I turned to June. She smiled.

segments.speaker: JUNE
segments.text: Absolutely. You're the funniest person I know.
segments.display: Absolutely. You're the funniest person I know.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I grinned. Then my phone buzzed. A message from Harper.
segments.display: I grinned. Then my phone buzzed. A message from Harper.

segments.speaker: HARPER
segments.text: Hey! Saw your audition. Really funny.
segments.display: Hey! Saw your audition. Really funny.

segments.speaker: HARPER
segments.text: One thing. We're adding a comedy montage to the assembly. Got any funny clips? Something that would really get people laughing?
segments.display:
One thing. We're adding a comedy montage to the
assembly. Got any funny clips? Something that would really get people laughing?

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I thought about it. I had plenty of funny videos. Mostly of myself falling off things.
segments.display:
I thought about it. I had plenty of funny videos. Mostly of myself falling off
things.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: But there was one video. One spectacularly funny video.
segments.display: But there was one video. One spectacularly funny video.

scenes.music: bright school-morning fanfare, upbeat marimba and claps, announcement energy

scenes.title: Two weeks earlier

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Two weeks earlier, June had sent me a recording.
segments.display: Two weeks earlier, June had sent me a recording.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: She'd been secretly practicing for the spring talent show. A dance routine. To a song she'd written herself.
segments.display:
She'd been secretly practicing for the spring talent show. A dance routine. To
a song she'd written herself.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: And let me tell you something about June Park. She was an incredible dancer.
segments.display: And let me tell you something about June Park. She was an incredible dancer.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: But when she got nervous, something happened to her arms that could only be described as inflatable car dealership man.
segments.display:
But when she got nervous, something happened to her arms that could only be
described as inflatable car dealership man.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: The video began with June wearing purple sunglasses in her bedroom.
segments.display: The video began with June wearing purple sunglasses in her bedroom.

segments.speaker: JUNE
segments.cue: to her phone camera, nervous but determined
segments.text: Okay. This is take seventeen. If this is bad, I'm joining the chess club.
segments.display:
Okay. This is take
seventeen. If this is bad, I'm joining the chess club.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: She spun. She slid. She attempted a move that looked like a malfunctioning helicopter.
segments.display:
She spun. She slid. She attempted a move that looked like a malfunctioning
helicopter.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: And then... crash. She disappeared behind her bed.
segments.display: And then... crash. She disappeared behind her bed.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Then one hand emerged from the floor and gave a thumbs-up.
segments.display: Then one hand emerged from the floor and gave a thumbs-up.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I'd laughed so hard I couldn't breathe.
segments.display: I'd laughed so hard I couldn't breathe.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: But June had made me promise something.
segments.display: But June had made me promise something.

segments.speaker: JUNE
segments.text: Nobody sees this, Milo. Seriously. I'm already terrified of performing in front of people.
segments.display:
Nobody sees this, Milo. Seriously. I'm
already terrified of performing in front of people.

segments.speaker: JUNE
segments.text: And don't send it to anyone.
segments.display: And don't send it to anyone.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Standing in the hallway now, I opened our messages.
segments.display: Standing in the hallway now, I opened our messages.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: The thumbnail stared back at me. Purple sunglasses. Helicopter arms. The funniest twenty-three seconds ever recorded.
segments.display:
The thumbnail stared back at me. Purple sunglasses. Helicopter arms. The
funniest twenty-three seconds ever recorded.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I could practically hear the assembly laughing. I could picture Harper congratulating me. I could picture everyone finally forgetting Juice Boy.
segments.display:
I could practically hear the assembly laughing. I could picture Harper
congratulating me. I could picture everyone finally forgetting Juice Boy.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: My thumb hovered over the video.
segments.display: My thumb hovered over the video.

segments.speaker: HARPER
segments.text: Oh. My. God. Milo. This is gold.
segments.display: Oh. My. God. Milo. This is gold.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Then my stomach tightened. Just a little.
segments.display: Then my stomach tightened. Just a little.

scenes.music: sneaky, quirky flashback cue, muted trumpet and bassoon, a little goofy, bedroom dance energy

scenes.title: Lunch

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: By lunch, things were going better than I'd imagined.
segments.display: By lunch, things were going better than I'd imagined.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: She gave me a high five. An actual high five. From Harper Blake. At our lunch table.
segments.display:
She gave me a high five. An actual high five. From Harper Blake. At our lunch
table.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Across from me, June nearly choked on a french fry.
segments.display: Across from me, June nearly choked on a french fry.

segments.speaker: HARPER
segments.text: You're definitely one of my favorites. That clip? Hilarious. We're using it in the assembly.
segments.display:
You're definitely one of my favorites. That clip? Hilarious. We're
using it in the assembly.

segments.speaker: HARPER
segments.text: Yeah! Right before we announce the new host. It's going to kill.
segments.display:
Yeah! Right before we announce the new
host. It's going to kill.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: She walked away. June looked at me.
segments.display: She walked away. June looked at me.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I tried to laugh. It sounded like a lawn mower failing to start.
segments.display: I tried to laugh. It sounded like a lawn mower failing to start.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: She blinked. For one second, I thought she'd laugh.
segments.display: She blinked. For one second, I thought she'd laugh.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Instead, her face changed. Not angry. Worse. Hurt.
segments.display: Instead, her face changed. Not angry. Worse. Hurt.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Around us, the cafeteria continued its usual chaos. Someone launched a grape across the room.
segments.display:
Around us, the cafeteria continued its usual chaos. Someone launched a grape
across the room.

segments.speaker: KID
segments.cue: loud and indignant, far across the cafeteria

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: But at our table, everything had gone quiet.
segments.display: But at our table, everything had gone quiet.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I thought it might help me win.
segments.display: I thought it might help me win.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: June stared at me. Then she picked up her tray.
segments.display: June stared at me. Then she picked up her tray.

segments.speaker: JUNE
segments.text: You know why I sent you that video?
segments.display: You know why I sent you that video?

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: To see if the dance was good.
segments.display: To see if the dance was good.

segments.speaker: JUNE
segments.text: Because I was scared. And you always make scary things feel less scary.
segments.display:
Because I was scared. And you always make scary
things feel less scary.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I sat there holding a french fry.
segments.display: I sat there holding a french fry.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: It was probably the worst french fry of my entire life.
segments.display: It was probably the worst french fry of my entire life.

scenes.music: cheerful cafeteria bustle cue that slowly turns uneasy, light percussion, a wrong note creeping in

scenes.title: 1:45 p.m.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: At 1:45, I had forty-five minutes to save my friendship.
segments.display: At 1:45, I had forty-five minutes to save my friendship.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Unfortunately, I had absolutely no idea how.
segments.display: Unfortunately, I had absolutely no idea how.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I found Harper backstage in the auditorium, checking her notes.
segments.display: I found Harper backstage in the auditorium, checking her notes.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: My throat went dry. I imagined telling her the truth.
segments.display: My throat went dry. I imagined telling her the truth.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: Hey, Harper. That video I sent you? I wasn't supposed to. My best friend trusted me, and I used it to get your attention.
segments.display:
Hey, Harper. That video I sent you? I wasn't supposed to. My best friend

segments.speaker: MILO

segments.display: Then I imagined her face. Her disappointment. The hosting job disappearing.

segments.speaker: HARPER
segments.text: Actually, could you help check the montage? The tech club loaded everything already.
segments.display:
Actually, could you help check the montage? The tech club loaded

segments.speaker: MILO

segments.display:
I glanced at the screen. There it was. A folder labeled Friday Showcase Final.
Inside was a file called June Dance Final.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: I had two choices. Tell Harper the truth. Or somehow delete the video.
segments.display: I had two choices. Tell Harper the truth. Or somehow delete the video.

segments.text: I looked around. Nobody was watching.
segments.display: I looked around. Nobody was watching.

segments.text: I walked to the laptop. Clicked the file. Dragged it toward the trash. And...
segments.display: I walked to the laptop. Clicked the file. Dragged it toward the trash. And...

segments.display:
I jumped. My elbow hit a plastic cup sitting beside the keyboard. The cup

segments.text: Then, from somewhere behind the curtain, a voice yelled:
segments.display: Then, from somewhere behind the curtain, a voice yelled:

scenes.title: 2:25 p.m.

segments.speaker: MILO
segments.text: The projector still wasn't working. Mr. Alvarez, our technology teacher, was crouched behind the stage muttering words that definitely weren't in the school handbook.
segments.display:
The projector still wasn't working. Mr. Alvarez, our technology teacher, was

And I was sitting in the front row, wondering whether changing my name and

At 2:29, the projector flickered back to life. The auditorium cheered. Mr.

All right, Wildcats! Who's

Before we announce our next Wildcat Weekly

I wanted everyone to think I was funny. And
